newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sept housing completions fell 5.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sept housing completions fell 5.8 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department report on completions of new privately-owned housing units, seasonally adjusted annual rates, in 1,000s, with percent changes from prior months and year over year.
Housing completions by region, seasonally adj., in 1,000s:
The 5.8 percent drop in September housing completions was the biggest decline since a 9.9 percent fall in December 1995.

Completions of single-family homes fell 4.2 percent in September after August was revised to a 0.7 percent rise, and July revised to a 1.5 percent increase. Previously, the department said single-family completions fell 1.3 percent in August and rose 1.2 percent in July.

September multi-family unit completions fell 12.5 percent after a 4.3 percent drop in August and a revised 4.1 percent increase in July. Previously, the department said July multi-family unit completions rose 5.2 percent.

The department said actual completions on an unadjusted basis fell in September to 119,400 units from 132,900 units in August and 126,300 units in July. In September last year, actual completions were reported at 115,500.

Privately-owned housing units under construction rose to a seasonally adjusted 836,000 in September from 824,000 in August and 823,000 in July. They compare with 783,000 units under construction in September last year.
